title: The coin game with an infinite average

probes.question: Why is the St. Petersburg game called a paradox?
options: Its expected payoff is infinite, yet it seems worth very little

probes.question: True or false: the problem was invented by Daniel Bernoulli.

image.alt: Sepia portrait of Daniel Bernoulli in a powdered wig and velvet coat.

body.question: A fair coin is flipped until it lands heads. You win $2 if heads comes first, $4 if it comes second, $8 if third, doubling each time. What is the expected payoff?
body.reveal: Infinite. Each possible ending adds $1 on average (half the chance, double the prize, and so on), and the stages never stop. Yet few people would pay even $25 to play. That gap is the St. Petersburg paradox.
